technology.summary: Today's technology news includes Microsoft's announcement of its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip, which will improve the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud. Meanwhile, Amazon has over 1 million robot workers, raising questions about the future of human employees. In other news, a former Plaud executive has raised $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background, and Fitbit has officially launched the Fitbit Edge, a fitness tracker for those who want notifications without a screen.

finance.summary: Today's most important finance news includes a decline in benchmark indices due to global uncertainty and cautious investor sentiment, with the Nifty index under pressure and foreign portfolio investors recording net sales. Indian equity benchmarks also experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. A resurgent El Niño pattern may deepen a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, pushing yields higher. The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have joined forces to simplify regulatory procedures for foreign portfolio investors, with the India Market Access portal launching in September 2025.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for a SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court is set to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, claiming that his ability to execute illegal orders makes him a liability for the country. Meanwhile, Congress has condemned the detention of tribal students who were headed to Mumbai to protest.

In other news, former US President Donald Trump has cited a non-existent Indian election to call the US electoral process 'corrupt'. India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly dropped by $18.34 billion in a single week. Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
